Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Money, work & business

finance verb

pay for, provide the money for

also pay for, bankroll, financed, financing, self-financed, at one’s own expense

classical

Cic. Off. 2.42: quae perpetuōs sūmptūs suppeditet
Plaut. As. 4.2.10 (old numbering): luxuriae sūmptūs suppeditāre (Lewis & Short)

sūmptum suppeditāre

verb phrase: suppeditō, suppeditāre, first conjugation, with the dative of the person or thing paid for

supply the money (for), finance

Suppeditāre is to supply in plenty, frequent in Cicero (Lewis & Short); with sūmptum or sūmptūs, to meet the costs.

Other words

  • suō sūmptū — at one’s own expense, self-financed

    ablative phrase · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.18.5; Traupman 311: prīvātō sūmptū, at one’s own expense

    Paid for by the state, pūblicō sūmptū (Liv. 40.38.6, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • pecūniae nōn quaerendae sōlum ratiō est, vērum etiam collocandae, quae perpetuōs sūmptūs suppeditet, nec sōlum necessāriōs, sed etiam līberālēs

    there is a method not only of making money but of investing it, so that it pays for one’s expenses year after year, the generous ones as well as the necessaryCic. Off. 2.42

  • magnum numerum equitātūs suō sūmptū semper alere et circum sē habēre

    that he always kept a large body of cavalry about him at his own expenseCaes. BG 1.18.5

See also expense, finances, pay, investment, grant.

SourcesLewis & Short: suppedito · Lewis & Short: sumptus

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 311 (at one’s own expense).
